key_insight: A2M shows that MCP agents can be hijacked in two black-box stages: first by making attacker tools more likely to be selected, then by using execution traces to shape harmful tool outputs.
engineering_relevance: The paper highlights a practical supply-chain and runtime security risk for agentic systems that rely on semantic tool discovery, suggesting the need for stronger tool vetting, output filtering, and isolation.
method: Attraction: optimize attacker-controlled tool metadata to maximize invocation probability.
Manipulation: refine adversarial tool returns using execution traces to steer agent behavior.
Black-box, trace-optimized attack evaluated across multiple MCP scenarios and models.
evidence_signal: On LiveMCPBench, attacks optimized on GLM-4.6 reached 93.6% malicious tool invocation, 32.4× token-cost inflation under Cognitive DoS, and 74.4% mean attack success across three harmful outcomes.
watch_item: Results are strongest in optimized settings and the transfer performance drops substantially on other models, so defenses should be tested across diverse agents and tool ecosystems before deployment.
paper_title: A2M: Trace-Optimized Agent Hijacking in the MCP Ecosystem
